# Wayfinder 0.3.0
This release makes folders more personal and useful with folder-specific pins, properties, recent history, and related items. It also adds source-code previews and hidden-file support, alongside a substantial round of navigation, drag-and-drop, persistence, and visual improvements.
## A richer home for every folder
- Pin important files and folders inside a folder for quick access without moving or duplicating them. - Pinned items appear above the regular column contents and can be added from the file menu, by dragging, or with the Command Palette. - The folder Info panel now brings together custom properties and recent activity, and stays closed by default until you need it. - Related folders and URLs now sit alongside file-view tabs, making connected locations easier to reach without taking up a separate sidebar. - A consolidated Add menu keeps new files, new folders, file views, related folders, and related URLs in one predictable place.
## Source previews and hidden files
- The Inspector can now show fast, read-only previews with syntax highlighting for many common source-code and configuration formats. - Added preview support for Swift, JavaScript, TypeScript, TSX, JSX, Python, Rust, HTML, CSS, JSON, YAML, Astro, shell scripts, `.env`, `.gitignore`, and more. - Code previews follow the current Light or Dark appearance and clearly explain when a file is too large, unavailable, or cannot be previewed safely. - A new Appearance setting lets you show hidden files and folders throughout file views and search.
## Better file views and properties
- File views, their layouts, custom properties, and folder-specific pins now save more consistently across tabs, panes, and app launches. - Existing setups are carried forward automatically into the new file-view system. - Files now have clearer hover states and a quick-access three-dot menu for pinning items and adding or changing their properties. - Custom properties are easier to see and edit directly from column-view rows, with clearer colored badges and compact overflow handling. - Folder titles, file-view tabs, and related items have been streamlined into a cleaner, more consistent toolbar.
## Smoother navigation and drag and drop
- Dragging over a folder can now open it automatically, making deeper drop destinations much easier to reach. - The Shelf now expands and collapses more smoothly, has clearer hover feedback, and no longer interferes with ordinary folder drags or keyboard focus. - Newly pasted or added files receive clearer arrival feedback and selection changes feel more natural. - After deleting files with the keyboard, Wayfinder keeps your place by selecting the most useful nearby item. - Sidebar spaces remain stable while resizing, without jumping between pages.
## Fixes and polish
- Improved inline renaming, including more reliable focus and filename selection for newly created items. - Fixed several cases where folder state, selection, navigation, or property changes could be lost or applied to the wrong view. - Improved tab and pane presentation, including clearer active-pane styling and more reliable switching between previously opened tabs. - Refined popovers, row actions, pinned indicators, dividers, spacing, and selection animations across the app.

# Wayfinder 0.2.0
The release adds independent tabs in every pane, recursive splits, direct manipulation across tabs and the sidebar, deeper macOS integration, and a substantial round of navigation, performance, and reliability improvements.
## A new tabbed, multi-pane workspace
- Panes can be split repeatedly to the right or downward instead of being limited to a single dual-pane layout. - Tabs can be reordered live, moved between panes, or dropped on a pane edge to create a new split. - Tabs now open and close significantly faster - Reordering tabs is much more polished than before.
## Better macOS and Finder integration
- Wayfinder can now be enabled as the default folder viewer for supported Open, Reveal, and Show requests, with controls to enable, repair, or restore the previous handler. - Folders and files opened from Finder or another app are routed into Wayfinder's existing windows and panes.
## More capable sidebar drag and drop
- Sidebar folders can be dragged directly into the main window to create a split pane. - Pinned folders can now be reordered within a group or moved between groups. - Sidebar defaults and migrations have been tightened, including removal of only the legacy seeded Projects shortcut while preserving personal folders with the same name.
## Column view, selection, and Inspector improvements
- Column widths are now saved per directory. - An optional “Right-size columns to contents” setting automatically fits columns until a manual width is chosen. - Column view should behave more 'Finder-like' with it's logic for horizontally scrolling. - A new Preview preference controls whether a single selected folder opens the preview panel; files and multi-item summaries continue to open it automatically. - Folder navigation, selection restoration, and cached column state are more consistent when moving backward, forward, or between tabs. - Empty areas in column view now expose the appropriate New File and New Folder actions. - Renaming flow now consistently works as expected.
## Safer file operations and native interaction
- Copy and move replacements now use a transactional operation path that can undo and redo both the incoming item and the displaced destination. - Failed or cancelled multi-item copy, move, trash, and restore operations roll back completed work where possible and report partial state when a rollback itself fails. - Drag-and-drop now detects existing destinations and duplicate incoming names before committing the transfer. - Inline rename, copy, paste, cloud-status controls, and embedded column controls now claim keyboard and mouse focus without changing selection unexpectedly. - File-list and column-view commands now remain attached to the pane where the interaction began.
## Settings, appearance, and smaller refinements
- Added General settings for default-folder-viewer integration and choosing how externally opened folders are routed. - Added the column auto-sizing preference and renamed workspace restoration to “Restore tabs and panes on launch” to reflect the expanded behavior. - Added an option to show or hide the current folder title beside the file-view tabs. - Added a brand-blue sidebar selection style and separate Light and Dark appearance colors for the Related sidebar. - Popovers, menus, filter/sort editors, and settings surfaces have refreshed spacing, borders, backgrounds, and presentation behavior. - The sidebar eject control, inactive tabs, pane toolbars, dividers, selection colors, and narrow-window Inspector layout received visual polish. - Double-clicking the titlebar now respects the macOS preference to minimize, zoom, or take no action. - WebP conversion now matches `cwebp`'s default encoding behavior more closely.
